title: Most Maryland residents don’t want new data centers, UMBC poll finds
key_facts: UMBC Institute of Politics poll of 776 likely voters, 22 to 27 Sep, margin of error 3.5 points, released Thursday.
13% support new data centers in the state; 16% support them near their community.
Opposition cuts across party, gender, geography, age, education and income.
Gov. Wes Moore, previously a supporter, proposed review standards and a task force but no pause or ban.
Republican challenger Dan Cox now backs a moratorium on hyperscale data centers; Green candidate Andy Ellis wants a ban.
quote_evidence: The survey from the University of Maryland, Baltimore County’s Institute of Politics found that just 13% of respondents support new data centers in the state and just 16% support data centers being built near their communities.
He did not go so far as to propose a pause or ban on new data centers, as many local governments and some governors in other states have done.
why_it_matters_hint: Public opposition to data centers is now a central political issue in Maryland.
